links.outcome: Residual harm rates among cleared decisions by race/ethnicity and sex subgroup
links.effect: Baseline residual harm varied from 1.03% (Hispanic) to 1.33% (non-Hispanic black, p=0.006); female 1.14% vs male 1.28%.
links.quote: Baseline residual harm varied from 1.03% (Hispanic) to 1.33% (non-Hispanic black, p=0.006).

links.outcome: Subgroup disparity and policy value after constrained fairness optimisation
links.effect: Disparity reduced 37% (95% CI 22% to 48%) for race and 28% (95% CI 14% to 39%) for sex; policy value decreased 0.2%.
links.quote: Constrained fairness optimisation tightened harm rates to 1.10%–1.20% across race/ethnicity groups, reducing disparity by 37% (95% CI 22% to 48%) for race and 28% (95% CI 14% to 39%) for sex ( table 3 ).

links.outcome: Whether conformal clearance separates low-harm decisions from those needing human review
links.effect: 89.5% of decisions cleared with 1.22% residual harm versus 6.67% harm among flagged decisions (81.7% relative reduction).
links.quote: Residual harm among cleared decisions was 1.22% (95% CI 1.14% to 1.30%) vs 6.67% (95% CI 6.02% to 7.32%) for flagged decisions, an 81.7% relative reduction ( table 2 ).

links.outcome: Clinician reviewer ratings of overridden AI recommendations
links.effect: 23% of overridden recommendations rated well-matched, 57% plausible but suboptimal, 20% mismatched; care teams better addressed needs in 77%.
links.quote: Reviewers rated 23% (95% CI 17% to 29%) of algorithmic recommendations as well-matched despite override, 57% as plausible but suboptimal and 20% as mismatched.

links.outcome: Divergence between care team choices and AI recommendations across clinical subgroups
links.effect: Divergence higher for behavioural health (10.7% vs 6.9%, p<0.001), telehealth (11.2%) and ≥4 chronic conditions (12.1% vs 5.8%).
links.quote: Divergence was higher among patients with behavioural health diagnoses (10.7%, 95% CI 10.5% to 10.9%) than those without (6.9%, 95% CI 6.8% to 7.0%; p<0.001) and among those with ≥4 chronic conditions (12.1%, 95% CI 11.9% to 12.3%) than those with fewer conditions (5.8%, 95% CI 5.7% to 5.9%; p<0.001).

screen.practice: fairness-aware guardrails and conformal harm prediction gating
screen.reason: The study develops and evaluates mechanistic interpretability and fairness-aware safety guardrails (conformal harm prediction filter and clinician oversight) to mitigate harm and bias in an RL care coordination tool.
